content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To customize a drum set, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Apply base coat of lacquer to the shells (24 hours)
Step 2. Measure and mark holes for the new tom mounts (30 minutes)
Step 3. Attach custom brass badges to the snare drum (20 minutes)
Step 4. Buff the badges to a high shine (15 minutes)
Step 5. Install internal muffling systems (1 hour)
Step 6. Thread tension rods into the new lugs (45 minutes)
Step 7. Condition the bearing edges with paraffin wax (20 minutes)
Step 8. Apply manufacturer decals to the resonant heads (10 minutes)
Step 9. Mount the chrome floor tom brackets (40 minutes)
Step 10. Degrease the vintage throw-off mechanism (15 minutes)
Step 11. Seat the new drum heads on the rims (10 minutes)
Step 12. Clean the interior of the wooden shells (30 minutes)
Step 13. Install the vent hole grommets (15 minutes)
Step 14. Polish the exterior shell finish (2 hours)
Step 15. Lubricate the lug swivel nuts (25 minutes)
Step 16. Inspect shells for structural integrity (1 hour)
Step 17. Sand down the old wrap adhesive (3 hours)
Step 18. Draft the custom lug placement template (1 hour)
Step 19. Inventory all hardware components (30 minutes)
Step 20. Order specialty moisture-resistant gaskets (2 days)
Step 21. Vacuum out sawdust from the shell interiors (10 minutes)
Step 22. Select the wood grain orientation for the veneer (45 minutes)
Step 23. Level the bearing edges on a sanding table (2 hours)
Step 24. Drill holes for the bass drum spurs (30 minutes)
Step 25. Remove all old hardware and screws (2 hours)
Step 26. Research historical drum finish patterns (4 hours)
Step 27. Purchase high-tension tuning bolts (1 hour)
Step 28. Cut the custom sparkle wrap to size (1 hour)
Step 29. Install the new lugs onto the shells (4 hours)
Step 30. Final tuning of the entire kit (1 hour)
Step 31. Wipe down the shells with a tack cloth (15 minutes)
Step 32. Label each shell by diameter and depth (10 minutes)
Step 33. Purchase premium snare wires (30 minutes)
Step 34. Measure the shell diameters for accuracy (20 minutes)
Step 35. Sketch the logo design for the kick drum (2 hours)
Step 36. Mask off the bearing edges for painting (1 hour)
Step 37. Apply a sealant to the inner plies (5 hours)
Step 38. Assemble the snare strainer system (30 minutes)
Step 39. Attach the tom suspension mounts (30 minutes)
Step 40. Mount the bass drum claws and hoops (40 minutes)
Step 41. Tune the resonant heads to a specific pitch (20 minutes)
Step 42. Install the bass drum spurs (20 minutes)
Step 43. Glue the new wrap to the shells (6 hours)
Step 44. Attach the memory locks to the hardware (15 minutes)
Step 45. Apply a second coat of protective wax (1 hour)
Step 46. Install the die-cast hoops (30 minutes)
Step 47. Source aged maple wood hoops (3 days)
Step 48. Trim the excess wrap from the edges (1 hour)
Step 49. Clean the chrome rims with steel wool (2 hours)
Step 50. Tighten all internal mounting screws (45 minutes)
Step 51. Check for sympathetic snare buzz (15 minutes)
Step 52. Balance the kick drum pedal tension (15 minutes)
Step 53. Engrave the owner's name on the rim (1 hour)
Step 54. Sort the tension rods by length (20 minutes)
Step 55. Apply contact cement to the shells (4 hours)
Step 56. Install the snare butt plate (15 minutes)
Step 57. Position the drum set on the rug (20 minutes)
Step 58. Photograph the shells before customization (30 minutes)
Step 59. Fit the floor tom legs into the brackets (10 minutes)
Step 60. Check the roundness of the shells (30 minutes)
Step 61. Deburr the newly drilled holes (30 minutes)
Step 62. Apply a light oil to the pedal springs (10 minutes)
Step 63. Choose the specific drum head ply thickness (30 minutes)
Step 64. Adjust the height of the cymbal stands (15 minutes)
Step 65. Install the air vents (20 minutes)
Step 66. Spray the final clear coat (12 hours)
Step 67. Strip the old drum heads (20 minutes)
Step 68. Hand-polish the brass hardware (3 hours)
Step 69. Order a custom-sized drum throne (5 days)
Step 70. Test the throw-off action (5 minutes)
Step 71. Apply a UV-protectant spray (30 minutes)
Step 72. Set the beater angle on the kick pedal (10 minutes)
Step 73. Sign the inside of the shell (5 minutes)
Step 74. Organize the workspace (1 hour)
Step 75. Counter-sink the screw holes (30 minutes)
Step 76. Seat the batter heads (15 minutes)
Step 77. Re-tap the lug threads (2 hours)
Step 78. Affix the bass drum port hole ring (15 minutes)
Step 79. Purchase a set of professional drum keys (30 minutes)
Step 80. Clamp the wrap while the glue dries (8 hours)
Step 81. Document the serial numbers (15 minutes)
Step 82. Attach the snare wires (15 minutes)
Step 83. Apply a logo sticker to the shell (5 minutes)
Step 84. Install the tom brackets (30 minutes)
Step 85. Sand the interior for a smooth feel (1 hour)
Step 86. Choose the color of the hardware (1 hour)
Step 87. Cut the air vent holes (30 minutes)
Step 88. Position the floor tom (10 minutes)
Step 89. Inspect the shells for flat spots (45 minutes)
Step 90. Mount the rack toms (20 minutes)
Step 91. Clean the bearing edges (15 minutes)
Step 92. Set up the complete drum kit (1 hour)
Step 93. Select the wood stain color (2 hours)
Step 94. Purchase high-quality cymbal felts (30 minutes)
Step 95. Buff the hardware to a mirror finish (2 hours)
Step 96. Apply a wood conditioner (2 hours)
Step 97. Print the assembly manual (10 minutes)
Step 98. Perform a sound check (30 minutes)
Step 99. Place the drum set in the studio (1 hour)
Step 100. Install the mounting gaskets (45 minutes)
